reason: I want to assemble the arm's framework first, since the upper arm and forearm bones meet at the elbow.
expectation: I expect a basic arm or joint framework, though it may still need cartilage and other parts.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage and joint fluid seem useful for smooth movement, but I want to put the bones together first.

effect: The bones form rigid supports, so the joint still needs a way for them to turn relative to each other.
reaction: The distinction between bending bones and movement at a joint is clear.
reason: Cartilage and joint fluid are the only offered combination and seem relevant to smooth joint movement.
expectation: I expect a smooth joint surface or cushioning assembly, though I don't know exactly how it will be represented.

effect: The cartilage and fluid form smooth joint surfaces, and the next goal is to join the framework and attach the muscles.
reaction: The explanation makes their role in reducing grinding clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should put the smooth surfaces onto the arm bones.
expectation: I expect a jointed arm framework, though it may still need ligaments and muscles.

effect: The joint surfaces let the forearm move relative to the upper arm, but the framework still needs a pulling force.
reaction: The distinction between allowing movement and producing it is clear.
reason: Ligaments are the only offered combination and appear to be the next part of the joint framework.
expectation: I expect the ligaments to help hold the articulated bones together, though the muscles will still need attaching.

effect: The ligaments hold the joint together, and the framework now has slots for the opposing muscle groups.
reaction: The bone-to-bone role of ligaments is clear, and the empty slots make the next step easy to understand.
reason: I'll attach the bending muscles to begin adding the opposing pulls.
expectation: I expect the bending muscles to fill the front-pull slot, leaving the rear-pull slot for the straightening muscles.

alternatives.reason: The straightening muscles also need attaching, but either muscle group seems reasonable to add first.

effect: The bending muscles are attached through tendons, and relaxing them does not push the arm back; the opposing muscles still need fitting.
reaction: The distinction between relaxing and pushing makes the need for an opposing pull clearer.
reason: The straightening muscles are the only offered combination and should complete the opposing pulls.
expectation: I expect the straightening muscles to fill the rear-pull slot and complete the arm framework.

effect: The opposing muscles complete the framework and can steady the joint as well as move it; coordination remains another job.
reaction: Holding a weight still while muscles pull was an interesting extension of the model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the bending muscles was most worthwhile because it clarified how tendons transmit a pull and why relaxing a muscle does not push the arm back.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the smooth surfaces to the bones felt least engaging because it was the only offered combination and its result was fairly predictable.

surprise.text: I was interested that muscles can keep pulling without shortening, such as when holding a weight still.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the purpose of each part was explained, although several steps offered only one combination.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the opposing muscles are coordinated. The final result raises that question after making their mechanical roles clear.
